A public library organizes books by subject and author. A catalogue helps readers locate a volume, check whether it is available, and discover related works. Explain how this system helps a small community.
A baker combines flour, water, yeast, and salt. The dough rests while fermentation produces gas, then heat sets its structure. Describe why both resting time and oven temperature affect bread.
A bicycle converts a rider's effort into motion through pedals, a chain, and gears. Low gears make steep climbs easier, while high gears support faster travel on level ground. Summarize the tradeoff.
A music ensemble rehearses rhythm, melody, and balance. Each performer listens to the others while following a shared score. Describe two ways a conductor helps the group coordinate.
A map represents roads, rivers, and settlements at a chosen scale. A legend explains its symbols, and a compass rose indicates direction. Explain why a useful map leaves out many real-world details.
A warehouse records incoming goods, their storage locations, and outgoing deliveries. Accurate records reduce lost items and help workers plan replenishment. Describe the role of consistent labels.

A bridge must support its own weight as well as changing traffic. Engineers consider material strength, geometry, maintenance, and weather when choosing a design. Give a concise explanation of these constraints.
A program can divide a large job into smaller functions. Clear inputs and outputs make each function easier to understand, test, and reuse. Explain this idea using an everyday example.
